answer: In a proof-of-stake-based Sybil resistance mechanism, validators must "forge" digital signatures to propose new blocks. To prevent fake identities, validators are required to "copper"-plate their stakes by locking up a substantial amount of cryptocurrency. This costly action makes it economically irrational for an attacker to create multiple identities, as they would need to replicate the expensive stake for each fake identity, much like attempting to craft an intricate sculpture from both valuable "copper" and rare "ivory".
